The t_llama_unit rows sit at exactly those four lines, one per platform block [config/test-benchmarks.json:149, :259, :330, :437]. The side branch d9e7645fee also leaves config/ untouched [git diff --stat c5d44bd86f d9e7645fee: 4 files, all h/ src/ t/]. The packer schedules from bench times [doc/slice.md:207, :433].

claims.claim: t/AGENTS.md asks for a refresh after adding or materially changing a test.
claims.evidence: The file says: "After adding or materially changing a test, refresh config/test-benchmarks.json with bin/slice bench --new or targeted bin/slice bench --update <name>." [t/AGENTS.md:23-26].

claims.claim: Commit 8887cbe37c ("refresh t_tool_call_serialize timings for the review fixes") is two commits before the branch point and shows the practice at this granularity.
claims.evidence: The base dd6e85226b is a merge commit whose second parent is 8887cbe37c [git show -s --format=%P dd6e85226b]. That commit changes config/test-benchmarks.json only, 2 lines in and 2 out [git show --stat 8887cbe37c]. Its subject is "chore(bench): refresh t_tool_call_serialize timings for the review fixes".

claims.claim: bin/slice bench --check only requires that a row exist on some platform, so CI stays green.
claims.evidence: cmd_bench_check exits 1 only for duplicate names or for "bench entries missing from every platform"; a row missing from the current platform is a warning [bin/slice:1966-1989]. CI runs --check in two workflows [.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:505, .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:361]. t_llama_unit has rows in all four blocks, so --check is satisfied either way. The PR also carries the repository default label Skip benchmarks [pr-body-live.md:133].

claims.claim: delphi-3bda is the granite_rapids_6962p block, already measured on.
claims.evidence: The JSON names the block granite_rapids_6962p with load_factor 0.978 and a 6962p t_llama_unit row [config/test-benchmarks.json:378-381, :437]. The PR body describes the unit-test and token-identity runs on delphi-3bda, an Intel machine with AMX [pr-body-live.md:113, :129]. The project memory records delphi-3bda as a 6962P [memory/MEMORY.md, entry "delphi-3bda hardware"]. The JSON itself does not name the host; the host-to-block mapping comes from these two sources.

claims.claim: t_amx_numerics only gained a 64-iteration fill on a 0.42 s binary, so it is not a material change.
claims.evidence: The added loop runs PAGE_TOKENS_64 = 64 outer iterations, each writing one 128-element row through append_v_row [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- t/t_amx_numerics.cpp, added lines 53-60 of the diff]. The 0.42 s figure is the genoa96 row, an AMD block where the AMX code is compiled out [config/test-benchmarks.json:152]. The 6962p row, the only block where the AMX path runs, says 0.903 s at 1 slice [config/test-benchmarks.json:489]. The conclusion (not material) still holds: a 64 x 128 element fill is far below one millisecond.

claims.claim: t_heap_v2 gained a single added CHECK, not a material change.
claims.evidence: The diff adds one assertion, CHECK(tron::is_aligned(live.get(), ARENA_ALIGNMENT_64)), plus two named constants and comment lines [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- t/t_heap_v2.cpp, added line 19 of the diff].

facts: Slice (bin/slice, the repository's test runner) packs the C++ test binaries onto machine slots using per-test timings stored in config/test-benchmarks.json [doc/slice.md:3, doc/slice.md:207].

The timing file has four platform blocks named genoa96, genoa32, granite_rapids_6960p and granite_rapids_6962p. Each block has one row per test with elapsed seconds and peak RSS (resident memory, in MB) at 1, 2 and 4 slices [config/test-benchmarks.json:3, :168, :273, :378].

The granite_rapids_6962p block is the one for delphi-3bda (the Intel test machine with AMX). Its t_llama_unit row holds 5.187 s, 5.256 s and 4.936 s at 1, 2 and 4 slices and 331 MB peak RSS, from a full bench dated 2026-09-20 [config/test-benchmarks.json:379, :437].

The PR adds two Catch2 test cases to t_llama_unit (Catch2 is the C++ unit-test framework): "packed V rows keep their bits through set_v, get_v and at()" and "append_v_row matches the independent packed-V formula" [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3461, :3693]. Together they add 275 lines in one hunk at the end of the file [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- t/t_llama_unit.cpp].
The PR description reports 20751 and 8192 assertions for these two cases, and 249115 assertions in 62 cases for the whole binary [pr-body-live.md:117, :121].
The PR changes 14 files. config/test-benchmarks.json is not one of them, so every t_llama_unit timing row predates the two new cases [git diff --stat dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f].
The test-folder rule says: after adding or materially changing a test, refresh config/test-benchmarks.json with bin/slice bench --new or bin/slice bench --update <name> [t/AGENTS.md:23-26].
The practice is in use at this granularity: the base commit's second parent, 8887cbe37c, refreshes only the t_tool_call_serialize rows (2 lines changed) [git show --stat 8887cbe37c].

bin/slice bench --update TEST benches only the named tests and merges the result into the JSON. Other rows and the block's load_factor are kept verbatim. The file is rewritten atomically. The post-bench calibration run is skipped on --update [bin/slice:6603-6608, doc/slice.md:468-475, bin/slice:2532-2540].

The bench measures each test at 1, 2 and 4 slices and runs one test per NUMA node (memory domain, one per CPU socket) at a time [doc/slice.md:447-452]. It launches the test under --instance i,n for every slot on both sockets, so it is a whole-machine measurement [memory/3bda-shared-with-bill.md:74-75].

CI runs bin/slice bench --check. That check fails only for duplicate rows or for a test missing from every platform block. A row missing from the current platform is a warning [bin/slice:1966-1989, .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:505, .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:361]. t_llama_unit has a row in every block, so CI stays green with or without the refresh.

Machine state as reported in the context file at 2026-10-06 23:30 UTC, not re-verified in this session: both sockets of delphi-3bda serve production (rinzler@0 and rinzler@1), and the nightly CI holds the machine from about 03:30 to 11:30 UTC [CONTEXT.md, R1 section]. No bench of the new cases has run. No timing for the new cases exists yet, so neither "unchanged" nor a delta can be stated.

The reviewer's 0.42 s figure for t_amx_numerics is the genoa96 (AMD) row, where the AMX code is compiled out. The 6962p row says 0.903 s at 1 slice [config/test-benchmarks.json:152, :489]. The added fill is 64 rows of 128 elements; t_heap_v2 adds one CHECK [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- t/t_amx_numerics.cpp, -- t/t_heap_v2.cpp].

options.label: A
options.what: Run bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit on delphi-3bda in the next free window after the nightly CI (serving stopped per the campaign protocol), commit the refreshed granite_rapids_6962p row as a second commit on the branch, and state the measured times in the PR description's Status section.
options.for: Satisfies the stated t/AGENTS.md rule exactly as the reviewer asked, matches the 8887cbe37c precedent, and gives Slice real timings for the longer binary. The --update path preserves every other row and skips calibration, so the commit is a 1-line JSON change.
options.against: Needs the whole machine (both sockets) while it is serving production and then held by the nightly, so the earliest window is after about 11:30 UTC tomorrow. Adds a commit after reviewers approved c5d44bd86f (the side branch d9e7645fee already does this, so the PR will carry a second push anyway).

options.label: B
options.what: Time t_llama_unit by hand on one socket (for example run the binary once under --instance 1,2) and, if the elapsed time matches the row within noise, write "unchanged" in the description without touching the JSON.
options.for: Needs no whole-machine window, so it can be done today. The reviewer explicitly accepted a description note if the timing is unchanged.
options.against: A one-socket single run is not the bench's 1/2/4-slice measurement under the bench's NUMA isolation, so "unchanged" would rest on a different measurement than the row. If the timing did move, the bench run is needed anyway. Weaker evidence for the same effort.

options.label: C
options.what: Leave the JSON for the next full bench (last_full_bench 2026-09-20) and reply that CI is unaffected.
options.for: Zero work and zero machine time; CI does stay green because --check only needs a row somewhere.
options.against: Ignores a written repository rule the reviewer quoted, and the precedent two commits before the base shows the team refreshes rows per test. Slice would pack a longer binary against old numbers until someone else runs a full bench.

draft.recommended: A: the rule and the precedent both point to a targeted --update, the measurement does not exist yet so nothing can honestly be called unchanged, and the PR will receive a second push (d9e7645fee) regardless, so the row commit costs no extra review round.
draft.reply: The rule holds. The branch leaves config/test-benchmarks.json untouched. The t_llama_unit row for granite_rapids_6962p still holds the 2026-09-20 timings: 5.19, 5.26 and 4.94 s at 1, 2 and 4 slices. No timing of the two new cases exists yet. I cannot call it unchanged today. bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit uses every slot on both sockets. delphi-3bda serves production now, and the nightly CI holds it until about 11:30 UTC. I will run the bench in the next free window and commit the refreshed row. I agree to leave t_amx_numerics and t_heap_v2 out.
draft.action: After the nightly CI releases delphi-3bda, stop serving per the campaign protocol, run bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit from the gen build, commit the changed granite_rapids_6962p row (config/test-benchmarks.json:437) as one commit on the PR branch, and add the measured 1/2/4-slice times to the Status section of the PR description.

findings.what: Two statements about the t_amx_numerics rows are wrong or unsupported. (a) "the 6962p row, the only block where the AMX path runs": granite_rapids_6960p is also an Intel Granite Rapids block (config/resource-map.yaml:155-160, model_pattern "6960P"), so AMX runs there too; it merely has no t_amx_numerics row (the test has rows only at config/test-benchmarks.json:152 and :489). (b) "an AMD block where the AMX code is compiled out": the test body sits under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:22 and :282), a CMake option that defaults OFF (CMakeLists.txt:46) and is ON in the preset (CMakePresets.json:68); the JSON records no build options for the genoa96 bench, so "compiled out" is not established. On AMD the AMX kernels cannot execute at runtime regardless of the build.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "The 0.42 s figure is the genoa96 row, an AMD block; AMD has no AMX, so the kernel path cannot run there whatever the build options. The 6962p row, the only Intel block that carries a t_amx_numerics row (the 6960p block has none), says 0.903 s at 1 slice [config/test-benchmarks.json:152, :489]." Apply the same wording in facts[11].

findings.what: "8887cbe37c is two commits before the branch point" is graded "holds", but the draft's own evidence shows it is the second parent of the merge dd6e85226b, and `git log --oneline dd6e85226b` lists it immediately after the merge (dd6e85226b, 8887cbe37c, 04fd6b8bfa, ...). So it is one commit before the branch point in log order; the reviewer's "two" is off by one.
findings.fix: Grade "partly": the commit is the base merge's second parent, the next entry in git log (one commit before, not two). The practice point stands: it changes only config/test-benchmarks.json, 2 lines in and 2 out [git show --stat 8887cbe37c].

findings.what: "cmd_bench_check exits 1 only for duplicate names or for bench entries missing from every platform" is incomplete. cmd_bench_check first calls _check_current_platform_bench (bin/slice:1917-1939, called at :1959), which also sets failed when the detected platform has no block, when its block lacks the tests/total_slices/load_factor structure (bin/slice_bench_data.py:78-87, is_platform_block), or when the current block has duplicate names. CI additionally runs `bin/slice bench --check-platform` with that same structural check [.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:488, .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:191]. None of these looks at whether one test has a row on the current platform; that remains a warning [bin/slice:1980-1985]. The conclusion (CI stays green) is unchanged.
findings.fix: Write: "bin/slice bench --check exits 1 for duplicate names, for a test missing from every platform block, or for a detected platform whose block is absent or malformed [bin/slice:1917-1939, :1959-1989]. A row missing from the current platform is a warning [bin/slice:1980-1985]. CI runs --check at gcp-nix.yml:505 and cmake-single-platform.yml:361 and the structural --check-platform at gcp-nix.yml:488 and cmake-single-platform.yml:191."

findings.what: "runs one test per NUMA node at a time [doc/slice.md:447-452]": the cited range covers the 1/2/4-slice measurement only. The NUMA sentence is at doc/slice.md:453 ("clean, only one test runs per NUMA node at a time during bench.").
findings.fix: Cite doc/slice.md:447-453.

findings.what: The evidence says "The JSON itself does not name the host; the host-to-block mapping comes from these two sources" (PR body and memory). A code-side source exists: bin/slice get_server_type (bin/slice:145-169) reads config/resource-map.yaml, where granite_rapids_6962p is selected by model_pattern "6962P" (config/resource-map.yaml:172-176); delphi-3bda has 2x Xeon 6962P [memory/delphi-3bda-hardware.md:12].
findings.fix: Add: "bin/slice picks the block from the CPU model string via config/resource-map.yaml:172-176 (model_pattern \"6962P\") [bin/slice:145-169]; delphi-3bda is a 6962P [memory/delphi-3bda-hardware.md:12]."

facts: Slice (bin/slice, the repository's test runner) packs the C++ test binaries onto slices using per-test timings stored in config/test-benchmarks.json. A slice is one FPGA (the accelerator card) with its share of CPUs and memory, the unit Slice schedules on [doc/slice.md:3-4, doc/slice.md:207].

The timing file has four platform blocks named genoa96, genoa32, granite_rapids_6960p and granite_rapids_6962p. Each block has one row per test with elapsed seconds and peak RSS (resident memory, in MB) at 1, 2 and 4 slices [config/test-benchmarks.json:3, :168, :273, :378].

The granite_rapids_6962p block is the one for delphi-3bda (the Intel test machine with AMX, Intel's matrix-multiply instruction set). bin/slice picks the block from the CPU model string through config/resource-map.yaml, where the block's model_pattern is "6962P" [bin/slice:145-169, config/resource-map.yaml:172-176]. delphi-3bda has two Xeon 6962P processors [memory/delphi-3bda-hardware.md:12]. Its t_llama_unit row holds 5.187 s, 5.256 s and 4.936 s at 1, 2 and 4 slices and 331 MB peak RSS. The block's last full bench is dated 2026-09-20 [config/test-benchmarks.json:379, :437].

The PR adds two Catch2 test cases to t_llama_unit (Catch2 is the C++ unit-test framework): "packed V rows keep their bits through set_v, get_v and at()" and "append_v_row matches the independent packed-V formula" [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3461, :3693]. Together they add 275 lines in one hunk at the end of the file [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- t/t_llama_unit.cpp].
The PR description reports 20751 and 8192 assertions for these two cases, and 249115 assertions in 62 cases for the whole binary [pr-body-live.md:117, :121].
The PR changes 14 files. config/test-benchmarks.json is not one of them. So every t_llama_unit timing row predates the two new cases [git diff --stat dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f].
The test-folder rule says: after adding or materially changing a test, refresh config/test-benchmarks.json with bin/slice bench --new or bin/slice bench --update <name> [t/AGENTS.md:23-26].

The practice is in use per test. The base commit's second parent, 8887cbe37c, refreshes only the t_tool_call_serialize rows (2 rows replaced: 2 lines removed, 2 added) [git show -s --format=%P dd6e85226b, git show --stat 8887cbe37c]. It is the next entry after the base in git log. So it is one commit before the branch point [git log --oneline -4 dd6e85226b].

bin/slice bench --update TEST benches only the named tests and merges the result into the JSON [bin/slice:6603-6608]. Other rows and the block's load_factor (the scale factor the scheduler applies to all timings in the block) are kept verbatim. The file is rewritten atomically [doc/slice.md:468-475]. The post-bench calibration run (a full-suite run that rewrites load_factor) is skipped on --update [bin/slice:2532-2540].

The bench measures each test at 1, 2 and 4 slices. It runs one test per NUMA node (memory domain, one per CPU socket) at a time [doc/slice.md:447-453]. It launches the test under --instance i,n (the flag that pins a run to slice i of n) for every slice on both sockets. So the bench is a whole-machine measurement [memory/3bda-shared-with-bill.md:74-75].

CI (the automated test jobs on GitHub) runs bin/slice bench --check. That check fails for duplicate rows, for a test missing from every platform block, or for a detected platform whose block is absent or malformed [bin/slice:1917-1939, :1959-1989, bin/slice_bench_data.py:78-87]. A row missing from the current platform is a warning [bin/slice:1980-1985]. CI runs --check at gcp-nix.yml:505 and cmake-single-platform.yml:361, and the structural --check-platform at gcp-nix.yml:488 and cmake-single-platform.yml:191. t_llama_unit has a row in every block. So the check passes with or without the refresh. The PR's Skip benchmarks label gates the perf-benchmark job, not this check [pr-body-live.md:133, .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:726].

The reviewer's 0.42 s figure for t_amx_numerics is the genoa96 (AMD) row. AMD has no AMX. claims.evidence: TRON_ASSERT expands to `if tron_unlikely (!(cond))` plus an abort call, so one assert is one compare-and-branch on the taken path [h/common/assert.hpp:69-81]. book::kv_block pays two such asserts per set_v or get_v call [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1557-1558]. The K route pays the same kind of check per token: page::k(slot, kv_head, i_page) indexes a two-dimensional view, whose operator[] asserts `data != nullptr` and `TRON_ASSERT_LT(i, d0)` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1869-1871; h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:72-75].

claims.claim: The description's reason "sat on a frequently executed path" is not backed by a measurement that showed the compare mattering.
claims.evidence: The removing commit's message says the instruction comparison "found one hot-path difference" and that "the refactor was no longer instruction-neutral there"; it names no timing [git show daf227de13, message lines 1-9]. The PR body says only that the assert "sat on a frequently executed path" [pr-body-live.md:105]. No TPS or cycle measurement of the assert alone exists in the PR evidence.

facts: Words used here: the packed V plane is the per-head value cache stored in VNNI order (Intel's Vector Neural Network Instructions layout, two tokens interleaved in one row). pair_base is the function that returns the address of the row that holds a given token. TRON_ASSERT is tron's run-time check; it stays active in release builds because the assert header undefines NDEBUG [h/common/assert.hpp:3-5]. One TRON_ASSERT is one compare-and-branch: the macro expands to `if tron_unlikely (!(cond))` and an abort call [h/common/assert.hpp:69-74].
pair_base at the PR head does no bounds check. Its comment says the page methods "already index inside the page" and that "page::set_v never checked it either" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:190-198].

page::set_v and page::get_v pass the token offset i_page straight into append_v_row and load_row without a test [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427, 2445]. book::kv_block asserts the page index and the KV head only, and never receives the token offset [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1546-1558].

On the model's save path, save_v_impl computes the offset as `tok.i - lo` from the page that holds the token, calls set_v, and only then calls mark_v_complete, whose `TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size)` runs after the store [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3165-3172; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1833-1835, 2002-2004].

On the copy path, page::copy_from asserts `src_begin + count <= page_size` and `dst_begin + count <= page_size` before the loop that calls copy_token [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2135-2138, 2127-2130]. So the copy route is checked before the store.

Two tests call append_v_row on a bare owner with no page: t_amx_numerics for tokens 0..63 and t_llama_unit for tokens 0..63 [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:227-233; t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3703-3709]. Only the loop bounds keep the token inside the plane there.

main's set_v did `kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[i_page / 2]` with no check [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2432-2439]. So the sentence "page::set_v never checked it either" is true about main and says nothing about the head.

Three comments in v_vnni.hpp describe history: "have always required" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:74-76], "page::set_v never checked it either" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:190-193], and "exactly as page::set_v always did" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:235-237]. At head, page::set_v is a one-line call into append_v_row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427].

pair_base runs once per row operation: once in append_v_row, once in load_row, twice in copy_token [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:245, 312, 356-357]. For a 128-dim row the loop below runs 8 iterations of 16 dims. Counted from the intrinsics in the source, the cheapest path (even-token bf16 append) issues 3 vector instructions per iteration, 24 per row, and the odd-token bf16 append issues 6 per iteration, 48 per row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:251-263, 267-278]. One restored assert adds one compare-and-branch to that. This is a source count, not a measured time.

The K save route already pays a per-token check. page::k(slot, kv_head, i_page) indexes a two-dimensional view, whose operator[] asserts `data != nullptr` and `i < page_size` on every call [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1869-1871, 2349-2352; h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:72-75]. save_k_impl calls it once per KV head per token [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3103].

The assert was removed by pre-squash commit daf227de13. Its message says the instruction comparison against main (Step F) found the assert "added a compare-and-branch to every page::set_v / page::get_v call and two to every token copied by book::append" and that "the refactor was no longer instruction-neutral there" [git show daf227de13]. The criterion was instruction neutrality. No TPS (tokens per second) or cycle measurement of the assert alone exists.

PR body line 105 says the assert "sat on a frequently executed path" and "The second commit removed it" [pr-body-live.md:105]. The first clause has no measurement behind it. The second clause is history, which the PR-description rule forbids.

Only then does it call mark_v_complete. mark_v_complete asserts `TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size)`, so the check runs after the store [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3165-3172; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1833-1835, 2002-2004]."

findings.fix: "Two tests call append_v_row on a v_vnni_tensor (the owner object that holds one plane's storage) with no page around it: ..."

findings.what: "intrinsics" and "dim" are undefined. The sentence "Counted from the intrinsics in the source, the cheapest path (even-token bf16 append) issues 3 vector instructions per iteration, 24 per row, and the odd-token bf16 append issues 6 per iteration, 48 per row" carries two claims with parentheticals. The odd-token bf16 append issues 6 per iteration, 48 per row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:251-263, 267-278]."

final.title: R2: pair_base - who proves token < Rows, history wording, assert or sentence

claims.claim: The comment's clause "whose callers (the page methods) already index inside the page" promises a check that no page method performs: page::set_v and page::get_v hand i_page straight to append_v_row and load_row.
claims.evidence: page::set_v ends in `append_v_row(kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v.as_view(), i_page, src);` with no test of i_page [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427]. page::get_v ends in `load_row(kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v.as_view(), i_page, dst);` with no test of i_page [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2445]. The comment text is at [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:190-193].

claims.claim: book::kv_block asserts the KV head and the page index only and never sees the token offset within the page.
claims.evidence: book::kv_block takes (slot, kv_head, pg). It runs three TRON_ASSERTs: the restore flag `reclaimable_kv_restore_attempt_ == 0` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1549-1550], `TRON_ASSERT_LT(pg, n_pages)` [1557] and `TRON_ASSERT_LT(kv_head, n_kv_heads)` [1558]. The reviewer's "two TRON_ASSERT_LTs" is exact. None of the three sees the token offset. page::kv_block takes (slot, kv_head) and forwards pageno() only [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2053-2058].

claims.claim: What proves the bound on the save path is save_v_impl's offset_in_page plus page::mark_v_complete's TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size), which runs after the store.
claims.evidence: save_v_impl computes `int j = pg.offset_in_page(tok_ix);` [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3165]. It calls set_v with j [3168]. It then calls `pg.mark_v_complete(slot, static_cast<size_t>(j));` [3172]. offset_in_page is the subtraction `(int)tok.i - (int)lo` with no check of its own [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1833-1835]. mark_v_complete asserts `TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size);` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2002-2004]. Every part of the sentence is verified. One route the review does not mention: page::copy_from asserts both ranges before any copy [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2135-2138].

claims.claim: The parenthetical is incomplete: t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:233 and t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3709 call append_v_row directly on an owner with no page.
claims.evidence: t_amx_numerics builds `v_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>` and calls `tron::append_v_row(v_owner->as_view(), t, ...)` for t in 0..63 [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:227-233]. t_llama_unit does the same with `v_vnni_tensor<ROWS_64, COLS_128>` for token in 0..63 [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3703-3709]. Only the loop bounds keep the token below Rows.

claims.claim: "and page::set_v never checked it either" describes the set_v that this PR deletes, so it is a regression argument and becomes uncheckable once set_v is edited.
claims.evidence: main's set_v addresses the plane with `kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[i_page / 2]` [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2432-2439]. There `v` is a raw array `bf16s v[page_size / 2][head_size / chunk_size * 2]` [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2346], so the index is unchecked. At head, set_v is a one-line call into append_v_row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427], so the sentence now compares the function to itself.

claims.claim: Line 74's "have always required" and line 237's "exactly as page::set_v always did" have the same history shape and are circular because page::set_v at head is append_v_row.
claims.evidence: The constant comment reads "page::set_v and page::get_v have always required head_size % 32 == 0" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:74-76]. The append_v_row comment reads "keep their upper 16 bits (truncation, no NaN correction), exactly as page::set_v always did" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:235-237]. page::set_v's body is the call to append_v_row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427].

claims.claim: pair_base is reached once per row operation (lines 245, 312, 356-357), not once per element.
claims.evidence: append_v_row calls pair_base once [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:245]. load_row calls it once [312]. copy_token calls it twice, once for the source and once for the destination [356-357]. The element loops below each call step 16 dims per iteration [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:250, 268, 282].

claims.claim: TRON_ASSERT_LT(token, Rows) would be one compare per 128-element row, on a call that already pays two TRON_ASSERT_LTs inside book::kv_block.
claims.evidence: TRON_ASSERT expands to `if tron_unlikely (!(cond))` plus a tron_abort call. So one assert is one compare-and-branch on the normal path plus a rarely executed abort block [h/common/assert.hpp:69-74, 80-81]. book::kv_block runs three TRON_ASSERTs per set_v or get_v call, two of them TRON_ASSERT_LT [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1549-1550, 1557-1558]. The K save route runs a check at the same granularity: page::k(slot, kv_head, i_page) indexes a two-dimensional view [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1869-1871], and view::operator[] asserts `data != nullptr` and `TRON_ASSERT_LT(i, d0)` [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:72-75], once per KV head (one key/value attention head) per token [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3100-3103].

claims.claim: The description's reason "sat on a frequently executed path" is not backed by a measurement that showed the compare mattering.
claims.evidence: The removing commit (682064f8fb on 2026-09-22, rebased copy daf227de13) says the instruction comparison "found one hot-path difference" and that "the refactor was no longer instruction-neutral there". It names no timing [git log -1 daf227de13]. The PR body says only that the assert "sat on a frequently executed path" [pr-body-live.md:105]. No TPS (tokens per second) or cycle measurement of the assert alone exists in the PR evidence.

facts: pair_base (the function in detail::v_vnni_access that returns the address of the pair row holding one token) does no bounds check at the PR head c5d44bd86f. Its comment says the page methods "already index inside the page" and that "page::set_v never checked it either" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:190-198]. A pair row is one row of the packed V plane (the per-head value cache stored in VNNI order, Intel's Vector Neural Network Instructions layout, two tokens interleaved in each 32-bit lane).

page::set_v and page::get_v pass the token offset i_page straight into append_v_row and load_row without a test [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427, 2445]. book::kv_block runs three TRON_ASSERTs (tron's run-time check) per call: the restore flag, the page index and the KV head (one key/value attention head) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1549-1550, 1557-1558]. None of the three sees the token offset. page::kv_block forwards pageno() only [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2053-2058].

TRON_ASSERT expands to `if tron_unlikely (!(cond))` plus a call to tron_abort [h/common/assert.hpp:69-74]. So one assert is one compare-and-branch on the normal path, plus a rarely executed abort block that loads the two operands and the format string. The macro has no NDEBUG guard. So it is active in release builds [h/common/assert.hpp:69-74].

On the model's save path, save_v_impl computes the offset as `tok.i - lo` (lo is the first token index of the page that holds the token) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1833-1835]. It calls set_v with that offset [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3165-3168]. Only then does it call mark_v_complete [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3172]. mark_v_complete asserts `TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size)`. So that check runs after the store [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2002-2004].

On the copy path, page::copy_from asserts `src_begin + count <= page_size` and `dst_begin + count <= page_size` first [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2135-2138]. Its loop then calls append_v, and append_v calls copy_token [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2127-2129, 2104]. So the copy route is checked before the store. The review does not mention this route.

The production load route is the hardware-attention page_info builder in full.hpp. It calls page::get_v with the offset `off`, which arrives as a parameter of the make_page_info lambda [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2739, 2759]. Its bound comes from the caller of make_page_info. set_v and get_v also have test callers in t/t_llama_unit.cpp (lines 142, 177, 711-718, 1104, 1123, 1857, 1877, 3134-3140, 3169-3171, 3298-3331), t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:684 and t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:106 (grep over h, src and t at c5d44bd86f).

Two tests call append_v_row on a v_vnni_tensor (the owner object that holds one plane's storage) with no page around it: t_amx_numerics for tokens 0 to 63 and t_llama_unit for tokens 0 to 63 [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:227-233, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3703-3709]. Only the loop bounds keep the token inside the plane there.

main's set_v did `kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[i_page / 2]` on a raw array `bf16s v[page_size / 2][...]` with no check [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2432-2439, 2346]. So the sentence "page::set_v never checked it either" is true about main. It says nothing about the head.

Three comments in v_vnni.hpp describe history: "have always required" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:74-76], "page::set_v never checked it either" [190-193], and "exactly as page::set_v always did" [235-237]. At head, page::set_v is a one-line call into append_v_row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2427]. The line-74 text belongs to the line-74 thread (R4). The R4 position drops the constant and both `% 32` clauses. On d9e7645fee that text has already moved into the append_v_row comment [d9e7645fee h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:221-223].

pair_base runs once per row operation: once in append_v_row, once in load_row, twice in copy_token [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:245, 312, 356-357]. For a 128-dim row (128 head elements) the loop below runs 8 iterations of 16 dims [250, 268, 282]. The counts here come from the intrinsics in the source (compiler built-ins that each map to one vector instruction). The cheapest paths, the even-token bf16 append and the even-token load_row, issue 3 vector instructions per iteration, 24 per row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:251-263, 315-326]. The odd-token bf16 append issues 6 per iteration, 48 per row [267-278]. One restored assert adds one compare-and-branch to that. This is a source count, not a measured time.

The K save route already runs a per-token check. save_k_impl calls `pg.k(slot, kv_head, j).set(kout)` once per KV head (one key/value attention head) per token [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3100-3103]. page::k(slot, kv_head, i_page) returns `k(slot, kv_head)[i_page]` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1869-1871], and k(slot, kv_head) returns the kv_block's k_view(), a two-dimensional view over the K array [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1862-1865, 2349-2352]. That view's operator[] asserts `data != nullptr` and `i < d0` on every call [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:72-75]. So the K side runs two compare-and-branches per KV head per token. The V side runs none.

The assert was removed by commit 682064f8fb on 2026-09-22 (rebased copy daf227de13, parent b951ba9b4c, on the branch history before the squash to one commit). Its message says the Step F check (the objdump comparison of wrapper functions compiled against main and against the branch) found that the assert "added a compare-and-branch to every page::set_v / page::get_v call and two to every token copied by book::append" and that "the refactor was no longer instruction-neutral there" (no longer the same machine instructions as main) [git log -1 daf227de13]. The criterion was instruction neutrality. No TPS (tokens per second) or cycle measurement of the assert alone exists.

The performance A/B (Step E of the test plan: main and the PR head run side by side, 36 runs, 12 of 12 cells inside the band, the allowed throughput difference) ran on 2026-09-22 on pre-rebase commit 682064f8fb, with the assert already removed, against main 0a51385e95 [pr-body-live.md:84-96 names no commit, memory i4525-first-3bda-test-campaign.md:3, 19-20]. The 2026-09-22 token-identity run used the first commit's binary (85084e937c, now b951ba9b4c), which still had the assert in pair_base [pr-body-live.md:80, git show b951ba9b4c:h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp has the assert, daf227de13 does not]. The 2026-10-06 token-identity run at c5d44bd86f ran without it [pr-body-live.md:129].

PR body line 105 says the assert "sat on a frequently executed path" and "The second commit removed it" [pr-body-live.md:105]. The first clause has no measurement behind it. The second clause is history. The PR-description rule (describe the head in present tense) forbids history in the body. Line 97 says "the refactor costs nothing measurable" [pr-body-live.md:97].

options.label: A
options.what: Restore `TRON_ASSERT_LT(token, Rows)` in detail::v_vnni_access::pair_base, before the return. Replace the comment at 190-193 with a sentence that names the assert and its cost. Reword 235-237 in present tense ("the conversion page::set_v performs"). Leave 74-76 to the line-74 thread (R4 drops it). Re-run the Step F instruction comparison (a compile plus objdump, no delphi-3bda slot needed). Rewrite PR body line 105 in present tense. It then says: pair_base asserts the token. The cost is one compare-and-branch per row operation plus the rarely executed abort block every TRON_ASSERT carries. The K route runs a bounds check at the same granularity. The A/B TPS band (main versus PR head throughput comparison) was measured on 2026-09-22 on 682064f8fb, without the assert, against main 0a51385e95.
options.for: Answers all three parts of the review. One check covers the page methods, page::copy_from, the full.hpp load route and the two direct test callers. The cost is one compare-and-branch next to 24 to 48 vector instructions per row (source count). The K route already runs the same kind of check per token. The two planes then follow one rule. The assert runs on every call. It is not dead code.
options.against: The three moved bodies (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, moved from kv_cache.hpp into v_vnni.hpp) stop being instruction-identical to main. The PR body must say so, and the re-run objdump supplies the exact instruction count. The A/B TPS band and the 2026-10-06 token-identity run were taken without the assert. The 2026-09-22 token-identity run was taken with it. So the body can state the cost only as an instruction count until jhan re-measures.

options.label: B
options.what: Keep pair_base unchecked. Replace the comment at 190-193 with a precondition sentence that names who satisfies `token < Rows`: save_v_impl (offset from the containing page), page::copy_from (range asserts before the copy), the page_info builder in full.hpp, and the test loops. Reword 235-237 in present tense. Leave 74-76 to the line-74 thread. Reword PR body line 105 to say the criterion was instruction neutrality and that no timing of the compare exists.
options.for: No code change. Every measurement in the PR body stays valid as is. Still removes the false obligation and the history wording.
options.against: Leaves the one route into the V plane without a check while the K route has one. The direct test callers stay unprotected. Answers the review's question with a sentence. The review suggested an assert instead and argued that its cost is one compare per row operation.

options.label: C
options.what: Option A plus a re-run of the A/B TPS band on delphi-3bda with the assert in place. The body's claim "the refactor costs nothing measurable" [pr-body-live.md:97] then covers the final code.
options.for: The PR body then carries a measurement for the exact head, not an instruction count.
options.against: Needs the whole machine after the nightly CI run. The nightly holds delphi-3bda from about 03:30 to 11:30 UTC. The R1 benchmark refresh needs the same slot. jhan decides whether one compare per row operation justifies the slot.

final.recommended: A. The review's cost argument holds: one compare-and-branch per row of 24 to 48 vector instructions (source count). The K save route already runs the same kind of check per token. The removal rested on instruction neutrality (same machine instructions as main), not on a measurement. So restore the assert and state the instruction cost plainly. C is A plus a TPS measurement, if the machine slot is free.
final.reply: page::set_v and page::get_v pass the offset through unchecked. The callers prove token < Rows: save_v_impl takes it from the token's page, page::copy_from asserts both ranges, and the two tests loop over tokens 0 to 63. I will restore TRON_ASSERT_LT(token, Rows) in pair_base and rewrite its comment. Cost: one compare-and-branch per pair_base call (two per token copy). The K save route already pays one per token in view::operator[]. The objdump comparison found the compare, not a cost. No timing exists. I will reword line 237 in present tense, re-run the comparison, and correct the description. Line 74 has its own thread.

quote:
Two things in these four lines. "whose callers (the page methods) already index inside the page" reads as an obligation the page methods discharge, but none of them does: `page::set_v` (kv_cache.hpp:2427) and `page::get_v` (2445) hand `i_page` straight through to `append_v_row`/`load_row`, and `book::kv_block` asserts `kv_head` and the page index only — it never sees the token offset within the page. What actually proves the bound is `save_v_impl`'s `offset_in_page` (model.hpp:3165) together with `page::mark_v_complete`'s own `TRON_ASSERT_LT(offset, page_size)`, which runs after the store rather than before it; and the parenthetical is already incomplete, since t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:233 and t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3709 call `append_v_row` directly on an owner with no page involved. Please state `token < Rows` as a precondition of this accessor and name who satisfies it, rather than implying a check exists upstream.

Second, "and page::set_v never checked it either" is a statement about the `set_v` this PR deletes. It answers "is this a regression?", which is a question for the PR thread, and it stops being checkable the moment someone edits `set_v`. The same shape recurs twice more in this header — line 74's "have always required" and line 237's "exactly as page::set_v always did" — and both are now circular, since `page::set_v` at head *is* `append_v_row`.

A question rather than a request: the description removes the assert because it "sat on a frequently executed path", but `pair_base` is reached once per row operation (lines 245, 312, 356-357), not once per element, so `TRON_ASSERT_LT(token, Rows)` would be one compare per 128-element row, on a call that already pays two `TRON_ASSERT_LT`s inside `book::kv_block`. If the instruction comparison showed that compare mattering, it is worth saying where; otherwise the precondition could be an assert instead of a sentence, and it would cover the direct test callers too.

findings.what: "its constructor is constexpr" is presented as an obstacle to validating inside view. The project compiles with CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23 (CMakeLists.txt:54). Under C++23 (P2448R2) a constexpr function may call a non-constexpr function such as is_aligned (reinterpret_cast at h/common/memory.hpp:96) as long as no constant evaluation reaches that call, and a one-line `if (!std::is_constant_evaluated())` guard removes even that risk. No constant-evaluated construction of an aligned view exists in h/ or src/ (grep for `constexpr .*view<` finds only a variable-template specialization at host_matvec.hpp:104). The reviewer will know this and will read the sentence as a weak excuse.

final.title: R3: the aligned flag is asserted nowhere

claims.claim: const_v_row_view and v_row_view hard-code VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE at lines 204 and 207.
claims.evidence: Line 204 reads `using const_v_row_view = const_view<T, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, Dma, seq<Cols>, sseq<1>>;` and line 207 reads `using v_row_view = view<T, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, Dma, seq<Cols>, sseq<1>>;` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:204, 207]. VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE is `inline constexpr bool VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE = true;` [h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp:24].

claims.claim: v_source_row and v_destination_row set that flag on whatever pointer they receive, and view's constructor `explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr)` inspects nothing.
claims.evidence: v_source_row returns `const_v_row_view<T, Cols, Dma>{row}` and v_destination_row returns `v_row_view<T, Cols, Dma>{row}` with no check [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:213-214, 219-220]. The one-dimensional view constructor is `explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr) noexcept : data(data) {}` [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:124-126]. The multi-dimensional one is the same [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:42-44]. The helpers' own comment says so: "These helpers neither check alignment nor copy data." [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:209-210].

claims.claim: The flag matters for correctness (the reviewer's phrase: "load-bearing"): append_v_row and load_row use the alignment-requiring intrinsics _mm512_load_ps, _mm256_load_epi32, _mm512_store_si512, _mm256_store_si256.
claims.evidence: On the caller's row, append_v_row uses `_mm256_load_epi32(vout_ptr + i)` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:253, 256, 269, 285] and `_mm512_load_ps(vout_ptr + i)` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:260, 289]. load_row uses `_mm512_store_ps(vout_ptr + i, ...)` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:321, 335] and `_mm256_store_si256(...)` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:324, 338]. One nuance: `_mm512_store_si512(v_ptr + ...)` writes the packed plane, not the caller's row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:263, 277, 297]. The plane's alignment is static [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:178].

claims.claim: The aligned parameter has never been validated anywhere.
claims.evidence: view.hpp carries the TODO "If a view purports to be aligned, validate that all strides except the last are multiples of (alignment/sizeof(T))" [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:13-15]. The flag only selects aligned or unaligned instructions. For float chunk loads: `chunky<float, true>` uses tron_mm_load_ps and `chunky<float, false>` uses tron_mm_loadu_ps [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:29-45]. For 256-bit bf16 helpers: `if constexpr (aligned) { return _mm256_load_si256(x); } else { return _mm256_loadu_si256(x); }` [h/tron/simd/aligned.hpp:14-18]. The bf16 and fp16 chunk loaders follow the flag the same way: the true specializations call tron_mm_load_bf16 / tron_mm_load_fp16, which auto.hpp defines as _mm256_load_si256, and the false ones call the loadu forms [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:49-92, h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:35-36, 43-44]. A tree-wide grep finds is_aligned used only in threading.hpp and one test, never in view or tensor code [h/tron/threading.hpp:372, 511, t/t_heap_v2.cpp:1220]. view.hpp is not among the 14 files the PR changes (git diff --stat dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f: 14 files, view.hpp absent).

claims.claim: Every other aligned view in the tree wraps storage whose alignment is a static property of the type (kv_block::k_view over alignas k, v_vnni_tensor::as_view over alignas data_), so these helpers are the first place a caller's raw pointer acquires the flag.
claims.evidence: The two named examples hold: `alignas(kv_block_alignment) bf16 k[page_size * head_size];` feeds `view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, ...>{k}` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2333, 2351], and `alignas(V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64) bf16 data_[Rows * Cols];` feeds as_view() [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:163, 178]. tensor and host_matvec do the same [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:34, 244, h/tron/kernels/host_matvec.hpp:88-89]. But main already builds aligned views from raw pointers: `eagle_f.set(const_view<scalar, true, true, seq<dim>, sseq<1>>(x_data));` where x_data is `const scalar*` [h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:1367-1369, same line 1369 on main dd6e85226b], `view<activation_scalar, true, true, seq<dim>, sseq<1>>(x_out).set(embedding);` where x_out is `activation_scalar*` [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3413-3416, main dd6e85226b model.hpp:3408], and dmatensor wraps `data.get()` from a DMA allocation [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:215-216, 219-220]. So the helpers are not the first such place. They are the first in the KV-cache path (the stored keys and values of past tokens) and the only ones with a prose contract.

claims.claim: t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:682 had to gain alignas(chunk_alignment) because a plain std::array<float, 256> was already fed to set_v's _mm512_load_ps on main.
claims.evidence: main has `std::array<float, 256> values;` passed as `values.data()` to set_v [main dd6e85226b t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:679-682]. main's float set_v uses `_mm512_load_ps(vout_ptr + i)` [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2523, 2532]. The PR head reads `alignas(chunk_alignment) std::array<float, software_geometry.kv.head_size> values;` [t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:681-682].

claims.claim: The production path is safe only by a second prose chain: full.hpp:2756 asserts in a comment that dest is 64-byte-aligned scratch, which holds because gof.cpp:203 declares alignas(64) v_scratch two files away.
claims.evidence: The comment reads "dest is page_info's caller-owned, 64-byte-aligned scratch" [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2756-2758]. gof.cpp declares `alignas(64) std::array<bf16, HW_MAX_KV_HEADS * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE> v_scratch;` and passes `v_scratch.data() + h * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE` [src/tron/gof.cpp:203, 213]. HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE is 128 bf16 values per head [h/libpos.hpp:72]. Each head offset is therefore 256 bytes. The other production caller, save_v_impl, relies on the executor's buffer type, which a comment names as btensor, htensor or tensor [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3155-3158, 3168-3170]. The float tensor is `alignas(chunk_alignment) std::array<element, d0> data;` [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:244]. btensor and htensor are dmatensor [h/tron/hardware/btensor.hpp:21, h/tron/hardware/htensor.hpp:8], whose alignment `std::align_val_t{chunk_size * sizeof(Scalar) * 2}` (64 bytes for bf16 and fp16) is requested from the DMA allocator [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:164-165, 171-172, 181]. The allocator is heap->allocate in production and aligned_alloc in the test shim [src/system/memory.cpp:461-468, src/pos/fake.cpp:440-444]. No runtime check exists on either chain.

claims.claim: A TRON_ASSERT(is_aligned(row, chunk_alignment), ...) in both helpers costs one branch per row. is_aligned is at memory.hpp:95 and is used this way at threading.hpp:372; chunk_alignment is 64, which covers the 512- and 256-bit forms.
claims.evidence: is_aligned is `bool is_aligned(const void* ptr, std::uintptr_t alignment)` returning `!(iptr % alignment)` [h/common/memory.hpp:94-98]. threading.hpp uses `TRON_ASSERT(is_aligned(end, sizeof(uint64_t)), ...)` [h/tron/threading.hpp:372, 511]. chunk_alignment is `chunk_size * sizeof(float)` with `#define TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 16`, so 64 bytes [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17, 51-52]. TRON_ASSERT expands to `if tron_unlikely (!(cond)) { tron_abort(...); }` with no preprocessor guard around it [h/common/assert.hpp:69-74], so the check is one compare-and-branch in release builds, once per helper call. One detail the reviewer did not mention: v_vnni.hpp does not include common/memory.hpp, and none of the 34 headers reachable from its include lines (walk over quoted includes under h/) does. The only includers are h/common/types.hpp, h/tron/threading.hpp and h/system/*.hpp. So the assert needs `#include "common/memory.hpp"` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:19-28].

claims.claim: Validating the aligned claim inside view itself is the better answer.

final.title: R4: V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32 has no reason left in the code

claims.claim: All three sentences of the comment above the constant describe the PR's development (what the old methods 'have always required', what 'the moved loops' do, and why the constraint was kept), and the middle sentence says the constraint is not needed.
claims.evidence: The comment reads: 'page::set_v and page::get_v have always required head_size % 32 == 0. The moved loops step one chunk (16 dims) at a time and do not need it. The constraint stays so that the accepted row widths do not change.' [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:74-76 at c5d44bd86f]. No sentence states what the constant means for the code as it stands.

claims.claim: V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32 is referenced only at its definition and in the requires clauses of append_v_row (line 240) and load_row (line 307).
claims.evidence: grep over h/, src/ and t/ finds the name three times: the definition `inline constexpr size_t V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32 = 32;` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:77], the clause `requires(Cols % V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32 == 0)` on append_v_row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:240], and the same clause on load_row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:307]. No other file uses the name.

claims.claim: page::set_v and page::get_v keep their own `head_size % 32 == 0` clauses as a bare literal at kv_cache.hpp:1912, 1920, 1929, 1938, 2425, 2443, 2460, 2477, so the rule is spelled two ways.
claims.evidence: The declarations carry `requires(layout_t::uniform_geometry && head_size % 32 == 0)` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1912, 1920] and `geometry.head_size % 32 == 0` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1929, 1938]. The definitions repeat them [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2425, 2443, 2460, 2477]. main (the base branch, dd6e85226b) has the same literal clauses on its set_v and get_v overloads [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1879-1929, 2435-2671]. The clauses are inherited, not new.

claims.claim: Dropping the two header clauses would change no accepted page width.
claims.evidence: The page methods call append_v_row and load_row with Cols = geometry.head_size and keep their own `% 32` clauses [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2425-2428, 2443-2446]. The software weighted sum accepts only head_size 64, 128, 256 or 512 [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2253-2254]. Every one of those is a multiple of 32. No instantiation that compiles today would change.

claims.claim: v_vnni_view and v_vnni_tensor static_assert only `Cols % chunk_size == 0` (lines 102-103 and 159-160), so v_vnni_tensor<64, 16> is a legal type.
claims.evidence: Both types assert `Cols > 0 && Cols % chunk_size == 0, "a packed V row spans whole SIMD chunks"` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:102-103, 159-160]. chunk_size is TRON_CHUNK_SIZE, which the code defines unconditionally as 16 [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17, 51]. The PR body says the same [pr-body-live.md:16]. Cols = 16 therefore passes the static_assert.

claims.claim: copy_token (line 352) has no width clause and handles such a plane, while append_v_row and load_row reject it, so the owner admits planes that two of its three bulk operations refuse.
claims.evidence: copy_token's template header and signature carry no requires clause [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:350-355]. Its four loops step chunk_size [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:362, 369, 381, 388]. The append_v_row and load_row loops also step chunk_size [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:250, 268, 282, 315, 329]. Nothing in their bodies needs 32, yet their requires clauses reject Cols = 16 [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:240, 307].

facts: v_vnni.hpp is the new header for the packed V plane. The packed V plane is the value half of the attention cache, stored with two tokens interleaved per 32-bit lane. append_v_row writes one token's row into the plane. load_row reads one row out. copy_token copies one token between planes. A requires clause is a C++ compile-time condition on a template. chunk_size is the number of fp32 (32-bit floating-point) values in one vector register. It is 16 in the current build [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17, 51, pr-body-live.md:16].
The constant V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32 is defined once and used in exactly two requires clauses, on append_v_row and on load_row [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:77, 240, 307].

The three-sentence comment above it says the old page methods 'have always required' a multiple of 32, that 'the moved loops' do not need it, and that it stays so accepted widths do not change [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:74-76].

The loops in all three bulk operations advance by chunk_size (16 dimensions) per iteration [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:250, 268, 282, 315, 329, 362, 369, 381, 388]. No instruction in the header needs a row width that is a multiple of 32 dimensions.
The owner type v_vnni_tensor and the view type v_vnni_view require only `Cols % chunk_size == 0` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:102-103, 159-160]. A plane 16 dimensions wide is therefore a legal type.

copy_token has no width clause and accepts a plane 16 dimensions wide [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:350-355]. append_v_row and load_row reject that plane [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:240, 307]. The type therefore admits planes that two of its three operations refuse.

The 32 once had a real reason. The first packed-V writer, set_v_from_vout in commit 40cb1c22a7 (2024-08-29, 'Speed up kv_cache scaled_v via striped bf16s'), consumed two 16-value chunks per loop iteration (`c += 2`). For that reason it carried `static_assert(head_size % 32 == 0)` [40cb1c22a7 h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:194-200, static_assert at 199, loop at 200]. `git log --reverse -S'head_size % 32' -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp` names 40cb1c22a7 as the first commit with that text. main (the base branch, dd6e85226b) has set_v loops that step 16 dimensions [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2442, 2450]. That reason no longer exists in the code.

The page methods page::set_v and page::get_v keep the literal clause `head_size % 32 == 0` in their declarations and definitions [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1912, 1920, 1929, 1938, 2425, 2443, 2460, 2477]. main has the same clauses [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1879-1929]. They are main's contract, not this PR's.

Only four head sizes reach the software weighted sum: 64, 128, 256 and 512 dimensions [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2253-2254]. The tests instantiate the plane as <64 tokens, 128 dimensions> only [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:377, 3703, t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:227]. Models take head_size from the plugin when it declares one, else dim / n_heads [h/tron/models/model.hpp:657-665]. The declared values in h/tron/plugins are 128 and 64 dimensions only [h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:147, h/tron/plugins/mock.hpp:90]. Every size in use is a multiple of 32. Removing the header clauses therefore rejects nothing that compiles today.

append_v_row, load_row and copy_token have one template each, with no second overload that the requires clause would pick between [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:242, 309, 352]. No test probes the width clause with STATIC_REQUIRE (the Catch2 compile-time check macro) (grep over t/ for MULTIPLE_32 or `Cols % 32` finds nothing). Removing the clauses therefore only widens acceptance.
The PR body does not mention the constant or a 32-wide rule. The body therefore needs no edit for this item [pr-body-live.md: no match for 'MULTIPLE_32' or '% 32'].

In the side branch d9e7645fee (the second reviewer's spelling-only edit, not yet pushed to the PR) the constant is gone. Both clauses remain as the literal `requires(Cols % 32 == 0)` [side branch h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:225, 292]. The three-sentence comment moved onto append_v_row, prefixed 'Cols % 32:' [side branch h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:221-223]. The reviewer's objection therefore still applies to that branch.

quote: All three sentences here are about the development of this PR — what the old methods "have always required", what "the moved loops" do, and that the constraint was kept so the refactor would not change behaviour — and the middle one says the constraint is not needed. What the constant means in the system as it now stands is nowhere stated; "the moved loops" names an event, not an invariant. It is also not the single source of the rule it names: `V_ROW_WIDTH_MULTIPLE_32` is referenced only here and at `append_v_row` (line 240) and `load_row` (line 307), while `page::set_v` and `page::get_v` keep their own `head_size % 32 == 0` clauses written as a bare literal (kv_cache.hpp:1912, 1920, 1929, 1938, repeated at 2425, 2443, 2460, 2477) — so the same rule is now spelled two ways, and dropping the two clauses in this header would change no accepted page width. What keeping them does change is the new type's contract: `v_vnni_view` and `v_vnni_tensor` static_assert only `Cols % chunk_size == 0` (lines 102-103 and 159-160), so `v_vnni_tensor<64, 16>` is a legal type that `copy_token` (line 352, no width clause) handles while `append_v_row` and `load_row` reject it. The owner therefore admits planes that two of its three bulk operations refuse to touch. Either state a real reason the row width must be a multiple of 32, in terms of the current code, or drop the constant and the two clauses and let `Cols % chunk_size == 0` carry it — keeping both plus a comment saying one is redundant is the worst of the three.

facts: Words used here: the KV cache stores the K (key) and V (value) vectors of past tokens for attention. The packed V plane is one page's V data in the VNNI layout (Intel's Vector Neural Network Instructions layout: two tokens share one 32-bit lane, the even token in the low 16 bits and the odd token in the high 16 bits) [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:40-44]. bf16 is a 16-bit floating-point format. v_vnni_tensor is the owner (it holds the bytes). v_vnni_view is a non-owning view of a plane; at(token, dim) returns one element of it.

The PR head c5d44bd86f adds the file h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp. The file does not exist on main dd6e85226b, so every line discussed here is new in this PR [git show dd6e85226b:h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp: path not in that commit].

v_vnni_view has two at() overloads. The writable one returns `T&` and is callable on a non-const view. The read-only one returns `const bf16&` and is callable on any view. Both check the token and dimension bounds with TRON_ASSERT_LT (an assert that stays active in release builds) [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:117-128].

The comment above at() says that writing through it neither clears the pair partner nor marks the token complete [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:113-115]. The pair partner is the other token of the same 32-bit lane. Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] in kv_cache.hpp requires that an even-token append zeroes its odd partner, so a NaN in an unwritten odd slot cannot leak into the weighted sum [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2228-2239].

Note [VNNI Packed V layout] ends with: "Direct element writes through a view (at()) do neither; they serve fixtures." [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:55-57]. Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] ends its invariant paragraph with: "Direct writes serve fixtures." [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2240-2242]. A fixture is test code that builds the data a test runs on.

No code in h/, src/ or t/ writes through at(). A grep for two-argument `.at(` finds two hits on packed views: the compile-time probe matrix_at_writes [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:112] and one read in the bit-pattern test [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3681]. The other hits are on the emulation matrix type in h/tron/emulation/, a different class.

The one read goes through a const-element view. The test writes `auto const plane = page->template v_packed<geometry>(slot, 0)` and then `plane.at(token, dim).to_bits()` [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3677-3681]. page::v_packed returns v_vnni_view<const bf16, page_size, head_size> [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1947]. So this read resolves to the read-only overload and would compile unchanged without the writable one.

The two test fixtures that build a plane use append_v_row, the bulk row write that applies the partner rule. t_amx_numerics fills 64 token rows into a heap v_vnni_tensor<64, 128> [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:227-233]. The formula test in t_llama_unit does the same [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3703-3709].

The only other whole-plane writer in the tree is book::fill_storage_slot. It takes the plane address through detail::v_vnni_access::plane and fills page_size times head_size elements linearly [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1653]. It does not use at().

The only reference to the writable at() is the probe at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:401. The probe is `requires(Matrix& m) { m.at(0, 0) = bf16{}; }` [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:112]. Three STATIC_REQUIRE lines (compile-time checks) assert that it is true for v_vnni_view<bf16, 64, 128> and false for the const view and for a const object [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:400-403]. v_plane_mut_t is defined at [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:376-377].

The B5 commit c12df586b6 (the answer to the maintainer's "100 LoC without any obvious users" comment 4134076112 at v_vnni.hpp line 104) removed the row type v_vnni_row and the expr base. Its diff trims "(at(), row[dim])" to "(at())" in the v_vnni.hpp Note and makes the same trim in the kv_cache.hpp Note. Both Notes keep "serve fixtures" [git show c12df586b6, v_vnni.hpp hunk lines 86-87 and kv_cache.hpp hunk lines 45-49]. The commit message lists "at() writes through a writable view and not through a const one" among the kept tested properties [git log -1 c12df586b6].

The maintainer's API sketch (PR 4424 issue comment 5765866077) had one overload, `T& at(size_t token, size_t dim) const noexcept`, which writes through a view of bf16 and reads through a view of const bf16 [issue4525/evidence/github-review.json, comment 5765866077]. So the writable at() traces to that sketch. The maintainer has not re-reviewed since the B5 commit [CONTEXT.md, People and state].

facts: The KV cache stores the K (key) and V (value) vectors of past tokens for attention. The packed V plane is one page's V data in the VNNI layout (Intel's Vector Neural Network Instructions layout: two tokens share one 32-bit lane, the even token in the low 16 bits and the odd token in the high 16 bits) [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:39-44]. bf16 is a 16-bit floating-point format. v_vnni_tensor is the owner and holds the bytes. v_vnni_view is a non-owning view of a plane. at(token, dim) returns one element of a view. A fixture is test code that builds the data a test runs on.

The PR head c5d44bd86f adds the file h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp. The file does not exist on main dd6e85226b, so every line discussed here is new in this PR [git show dd6e85226b:h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp: path not in that commit].

v_vnni_view has two at() overloads. The writable one returns `T&` and is callable on a non-const view. The read-only one returns `const bf16&` and is callable on any view. Both check the token and dimension bounds with TRON_ASSERT_LT (an assert that stays active in release builds: assert.hpp undefines NDEBUG (the macro that turns asserts off) at its top) [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:117-128] [h/common/assert.hpp:3-4] [h/common/assert.hpp:80].

The comment above at() says that writing through it neither clears the pair partner nor marks the token complete [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:113-115]. The pair partner is the other token of the same 32-bit lane. Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] in kv_cache.hpp requires that an even-token append zeroes its odd partner. Without that zero, a NaN (not-a-number value) left in an unwritten odd slot would propagate into the weighted sum [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2227-2239].

Note [VNNI Packed V layout] ends with: "Direct element writes through a view (at()) do neither; they serve fixtures." [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:55-57]. Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] has a two-sentence passage: "Direct element writes through a packed view (v_vnni_view::at) do not clear the partner, and no V write marks a token complete: the model calls page::mark_v_complete after set_v. Direct writes serve fixtures." [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2240-2242]. Once no view can write an element, the first sentence of that passage becomes false too, not only the last one.

No code in h/, src/ or t/ writes through at(). A grep for two-argument `.at(` finds two hits on packed views: the compile-time probe matrix_at_writes (a requires-expression that is true when `m.at(0, 0) = bf16{}` compiles) [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:112] and one read in the bit-pattern test [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3681]. The other 22 hits are on the emulation matrix type in h/tron/emulation/, a different class.

The one read goes through a const-element view. The test writes `auto const plane = page->template v_packed<geometry>(slot, 0)` and then `plane.at(token, dim).to_bits()` [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3677-3681]. page::v_packed returns v_vnni_view<const bf16, page_size, head_size> [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1947]. So this read resolves to the read-only overload and compiles unchanged without the writable one.

The two test fixtures that build a plane use append_v_row, the bulk row write that applies the partner rule. t_amx_numerics fills 64 token rows into a heap-allocated v_vnni_tensor<64, 128> (64 tokens by 128 dimensions) [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:227-233]. The formula test in t_llama_unit does the same [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3703-3709].

The only other whole-plane writer in the tree is book::fill_storage_slot. It takes the plane address through detail::v_vnni_access::plane and fills page_size times head_size elements linearly [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1653-1655]. It does not use at(). Both Notes already name book::fill_random as the one documented exception to the typed operations [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:50-52].

The only reference to the writable at() is the probe at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:401. Three STATIC_REQUIRE lines (compile-time checks) assert that the probe is true for v_vnni_view<bf16, 64, 128> and false for a const object and for the const-element view [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:401-403]. Their comment reads "A const view yields read-only elements; a writable view writes." [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:400]. v_plane_mut_t is defined two lines above v_owner_t [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:374-377].

Removing the writable at() closes the element-write path through a view. The raw-pointer path stays open: detail::v_vnni_access::plane and pair_base hand a bf16* to the named friends (fill_random, the AMX (Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions) attention kernel, the bulk operations) [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:182-198]. For those paths the partner-clear invariant remains prose, as the Note already says.

Commit c12df586b6 answers item B5 (the fifth item of the response page to the maintainer's review). The maintainer's comment 4134076112 at v_vnni.hpp line 104 reads in full: "It is a bit unfortunate that we grow this 100 LoC without any obvious users, but on the other hand it does seem useful." [exec/ben-20260930/review-comments.json]. The commit removed the row type v_vnni_row and the expression-template base class (a C++ pattern that builds array expressions lazily). draft.title: R6: "book goes through the typed operations" contradicts fill_storage_slot

claims.claim: book does not go through the typed operations: book::fill_storage_slot takes the plane address through detail::v_vnni_access::plane and fills page_size * head_size elements in a linear loop.
claims.evidence: At the PR head, fill_storage_slot writes `bf16* v = detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view());` and then loops `for (size_t i = 0; i < page_size * geometry.head_size; ++i) v[i] = ...` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1645-1657, worktree tron-issue4525 at c5d44bd86f]. One nuance: the other book method that touches V, book::append, does go through the typed route (book::append -> page::copy_from -> page::copy_storage_slot -> page::append_v -> copy_token) [kv_cache.hpp:1181-1210, 2112-2131, 2098-2109]. So the claim is exact for fill_storage_slot and the sentence is wrong for book as a whole.

claims.claim: Note [VNNI Packed V layout] at v_vnni.hpp:50-52 carves out book::fill_random as the one documented exception.
claims.evidence: The Note reads "book::fill_random is the one documented exception: it fills a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates." [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:50-52].

claims.claim: The comment on fill_random itself (kv_cache.hpp:1220) carves out the same exception.
claims.evidence: The fill_random comment says "This whole-block fill is the one documented exception to the typed packed-V access rule (see Note [VNNI Packed V layout] in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp)" [kv_cache.hpp:1217-1222].

claims.claim: The sentence at kv_cache.hpp:2248 is the only statement of the rule that overstates it, and a reader of scaled_v_expr will take it as the rule.
claims.evidence: The sentence reads "Page methods, book and tests go through the typed operations instead." with no exception named [kv_cache.hpp:2245-2248]. A grep for "typed operations" and "documented exception" finds only the three statements (1219-1220, v_vnni.hpp:50-52, 2248); the first two name the exception, the third does not. main dd6e85226b has no such sentence, so it is new in this PR [git show dd6e85226b:h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, grep for 'Page methods' returns nothing].

claims.claim: The preceding clause ("the one cache-side kernel that takes the plane address") is fine: fill_storage_slot is a fill, not a kernel.
claims.evidence: Callers of v_vnni_access::plane are exactly three: fill_storage_slot [kv_cache.hpp:1653], scaled_v_expr's initializer `data(v_vnni_access::plane(v_page))` [kv_cache.hpp:2257], and the AMX PV kernel `const bf16* const v_pairs = detail::v_vnni_access::plane(v_page);` [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:223]. The AMX kernel is not cache-side (it lives under src/tron/kernels), and fill_storage_slot computes no dot product. So scaled_v_expr is the one cache-side kernel.

facts: Words used here: the KV cache (key/value cache) stores one K (key) and one V (value) row per token for each attention layer. A `kv_block` holds 64 tokens of K and V for one KV head. The V plane is stored in the VNNI packed layout (pairs of tokens interleaved, so the bf16 dot-product instructions can read it in place). `v_vnni_view` is the typed view of such a plane, and `detail::v_vnni_access` is the one helper that turns a view into a raw address.

`detail::v_vnni_access` offers two functions: `plane(view)` returns the first element of the plane, and `pair_base(view, token)` returns the first element of the pair row that holds `token` [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:182-198].

`plane` has exactly three callers in the tree: `book::fill_storage_slot` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1653], the constructor of `scaled_v_expr` (the software weighted sum) [kv_cache.hpp:2257], and the AMX PV kernel `weights_times_v_128x4` [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:223]. No test calls it (grep over t/ finds no `v_vnni_access`).

`pair_base` has exactly three callers, all inside v_vnni.hpp: `append_v_row` [v_vnni.hpp:245], `load_row` [v_vnni.hpp:312] and `copy_token` [v_vnni.hpp:356-357]. These three are the "typed operations" the comments refer to.

The page methods reach V only through those typed operations: `page::set_v` calls `append_v_row` [kv_cache.hpp:2427], `page::get_v` calls `load_row` [kv_cache.hpp:2445], `page::append_v` calls `copy_token` [kv_cache.hpp:2098-2109], and `page::v_packed` returns the view itself [kv_cache.hpp:1950].

`book::append` (defragmentation copy between two books) goes through `page::copy_from` -> `page::copy_storage_slot` -> `page::append_v` -> `copy_token`, so that book method is typed [kv_cache.hpp:1181-1210, 2112-2131].

`book::fill_storage_slot` (random fill for tests, called only from `book::fill_random`) takes the plane address with `detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view())` and writes `page_size * head_size` bf16 values in a plain loop. It uses no typed operation [kv_cache.hpp:1645-1657, callers at 1227 and 1230].

Two of the three statements of the access rule name this exception: Note [VNNI Packed V layout] says "book::fill_random is the one documented exception" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:50-52], and the `fill_random` comment says the same [kv_cache.hpp:1217-1222]. The third statement, the sentence at kv_cache.hpp:2248 ("Page methods, book and tests go through the typed operations instead."), names no exception [kv_cache.hpp:2245-2248].

The sentence is new in this PR. main dd6e85226b has no `v_vnni_access` and no such sentence; its `fill_storage_slot` cast the whole block with `reinterpret_cast<bf16*>(&block)` and filled `sizeof(block) / sizeof(bf16)` values [git show dd6e85226b:h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, lines 1611-1619].

The tests reach V only through the typed operations: `append_v_row` [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:233, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3709] and the const `at()` accessor through `page::v_packed` [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3681 per the R5 facts; grep over t/ finds no `v_vnni_access`].
