final.title: R6: "book goes through the typed operations" contradicts fill_storage_slot

claims.claim: book does not go through the typed operations: book::fill_storage_slot takes the plane address through detail::v_vnni_access::plane and fills page_size * head_size elements in a linear loop.
claims.evidence: At the PR head c5d44bd86f, fill_storage_slot writes `bf16* v = detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view());` and then loops `for (size_t i = 0; i < page_size * geometry.head_size; ++i) v[i] = ...` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1645-1657]. One nuance: the other book method that touches V, book::append, does go through the typed route (book::append -> page::copy_from -> page::copy_storage_slot -> page::append_v -> copy_token) [kv_cache.hpp:1181-1215 (append, copy_from call at 1209), 2135-2158 (copy_from), 2112-2132 (copy_storage_slot), 2097-2109 (append_v)]. So the claim is exact for fill_storage_slot, and the sentence is wrong for book as a whole.

claims.claim: Note [VNNI Packed V layout] at v_vnni.hpp:50-52 names book::fill_random as the one documented exception.
claims.evidence: The Note reads "book::fill_random is the one documented exception: it fills a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates." [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:50-52].

claims.claim: The comment on fill_random itself (kv_cache.hpp:1220) names the same exception.
claims.evidence: The fill_random comment says "This whole-block fill is the one documented exception to the typed packed-V access rule (see Note [VNNI Packed V layout] in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp)" [kv_cache.hpp:1217-1222].

claims.claim: The sentence at kv_cache.hpp:2248 is the only statement of the rule that overstates it, and a reader of scaled_v_expr will take it as the rule.
claims.evidence: The sentence reads "Page methods, book and tests go through the typed operations instead." with no exception named [kv_cache.hpp:2245-2248]. A grep over h/, src/ and t/ for "typed operations" and "documented exception" finds five mentions. Two name the exception: kv_cache.hpp:1219-1220 and v_vnni.hpp:46-52 (lines 46, 49 and 51 belong to the same Note). kv_cache.hpp:573 (Note [Shared KV cache mechanics]) says packed-V storage goes "through the typed operations of h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp, see Note [VNNI Packed V layout]", so it refers the reader to the Note that names the exception. t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3688 is a test comment about append_v_row and at(). Line 2248 is the only statement that neither names the exception nor refers to the Note that does. The base commit main dd6e85226b has no such sentence, so it is new in this PR [git show dd6e85226b:h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, grep for 'Page methods', 'typed operations' and 'v_vnni_access' returns nothing].

claims.claim: The preceding clause ("the one cache-side kernel that takes the plane address") is fine: fill_storage_slot is a fill, not a kernel.
claims.evidence: Callers of v_vnni_access::plane are exactly three: fill_storage_slot [kv_cache.hpp:1653], the initializer of scaled_v_expr `data(v_vnni_access::plane(v_page))` [kv_cache.hpp:2257], and the AMX PV kernel `const bf16* const v_pairs = detail::v_vnni_access::plane(v_page);` [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:223]. The AMX kernel lives under src/tron/kernels, so it is not cache-side. fill_storage_slot computes no dot product. So scaled_v_expr is the one cache-side kernel.

facts: The KV cache (key/value cache) stores one K (key) row and one V (value) row per token for each attention layer. A `kv_block` holds 64 tokens of K and V rows for one KV head [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2333 (the K array), 2334-2338 (the V plane, owner type v_vnni_tensor)].

The V plane (one block's V storage) is kept in the VNNI (Intel's Vector Neural Network Instructions) packed layout (pairs of tokens interleaved, so the bf16 dot-product instructions can read it in place). bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating point format. `v_vnni_view` is the typed view of such a plane. `detail::v_vnni_access` is the one helper that turns a view into a raw address [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:182-198].

`detail::v_vnni_access` offers two functions. `plane(view)` returns the first element of the plane [v_vnni.hpp:184-188]. `pair_base(view, token)` returns the first element of the pair row that holds `token` [v_vnni.hpp:194-197].

`plane` has exactly three callers in the tree: `book::fill_storage_slot` [kv_cache.hpp:1653], the constructor of `scaled_v_expr` (the software weighted sum of V rows) [kv_cache.hpp:2257], and the AMX PV kernel `weights_times_v_128x4` (AMX = Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set. PV = the product of the attention weights with the V rows) [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:223]. No test calls `plane`. A grep over t/ finds no `v_vnni_access` at all.

The "typed operations" are four. Three go through `detail::v_vnni_access::pair_base`: `append_v_row` [v_vnni.hpp:245], `load_row` [v_vnni.hpp:312] and `copy_token` [v_vnni.hpp:356-357]. The fourth is the element accessor `v_vnni_view::at()`, which computes its address through the view's own private `pair_base` [v_vnni.hpp:120, 127, 143]. The Note calls them "the typed operations in this header" [v_vnni.hpp:46].

The page methods reach V only through those typed operations. `page::set_v` calls `append_v_row` [kv_cache.hpp:2427]. `page::get_v` calls `load_row` [kv_cache.hpp:2445]. `page::append_v` calls `copy_token` [kv_cache.hpp:2097-2109]. `page::v_packed` returns the view itself [kv_cache.hpp:1950].

`book::append` (the defragmentation copy between two books) goes through `page::copy_from` -> `page::copy_storage_slot` -> `page::append_v` -> `copy_token` [kv_cache.hpp:1181-1215, 2135-2158, 2112-2132, 2097-2109]. So that book method is typed.

`book::fill_storage_slot` (random fill for tests, called only from `book::fill_random`) fills the K array with a range-for loop. It then takes the V plane address with `detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view())` and writes `page_size * head_size` bf16 values (64 tokens times head_size dims, the whole V plane of the block) in a plain loop. It uses no typed operation [kv_cache.hpp:1645-1657, callers at 1227 and 1230].

The access rule is stated in three places. Two name the exception: Note [VNNI Packed V layout] says "book::fill_random is the one documented exception" [h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:50-52], and the `fill_random` comment says the same [kv_cache.hpp:1217-1222]. The third statement, the sentence at kv_cache.hpp:2248 ("Page methods, book and tests go through the typed operations instead."), names no exception [kv_cache.hpp:2245-2248].

A grep for "typed operations" finds two further mentions. kv_cache.hpp:573 (Note [Shared KV cache mechanics]) says book and page implement packed-V storage "through the typed operations of h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp, see Note [VNNI Packed V layout]" [kv_cache.hpp:569-574]. It refers the reader to the Note that names the exception, so it needs no edit. t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3688 is a test comment that says append_v_row and at() both compute addresses through pair_base [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3686-3690].

The sentence is new in this PR. main dd6e85226b (the base commit) has no `v_vnni_access`, no "typed operations" and no such sentence. Its `fill_storage_slot` cast the whole block with `reinterpret_cast<bf16*>(&block)` and filled `sizeof(block) / sizeof(bf16)` values [git show dd6e85226b:h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, lines 1611-1619].

The tests reach V only through the typed operations: `append_v_row` [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:233, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3709] and the const `at()` accessor on the view from `page::v_packed` [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3681]. A grep over t/ finds no `v_vnni_access`, so no test takes a raw plane address.
The reference to Note [VNNI Packed V layout] already sits on line 2247, the line directly above the sentence [kv_cache.hpp:2247].
The file's clang-format (the code formatter) column limit is 88 characters [.clang-format:85]. The three-line replacement comment measures 73, 75 and 83 characters, so it fits.

The side branch d9e7645fee (Wade's small style fix, the tree the next push carries) does not touch h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp. Its diff against c5d44bd86f lists four files: h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp, src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp, t/t_heap_v2.cpp and t/t_llama_unit.cpp [git diff --stat c5d44bd86f d9e7645fee]. The two kv_cache.hpp copies are byte-identical (checked with cmp, the byte-compare tool). So lines 573, 1220, 1653, 2247 and 2248 keep their numbers.

options.label: A
options.what: Keep the sentence and make it exact: name book::append instead of the word book alone, and add the fill_random exception with a reference to Note [VNNI Packed V layout], in the Note's own wording. Replacement for line 2248 (three comment lines): "Page methods, book::append and tests go through the typed operations instead. book::fill_random is the one documented exception: it fills a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates (Note [VNNI Packed V layout])."
options.for: All three statements of the rule then agree, word for word on the exception. The reader of scaled_v_expr gets the complete rule without opening v_vnni.hpp. Every name in the sentence is checked true against the callers of plane and pair_base.
options.against: The comment grows by two lines. It repeats one sentence that already lives in two other places.

options.label: B
options.what: Drop "book" from the sentence: "Page methods and tests go through the typed operations instead."
options.for: Smallest edit, one word removed, no repetition. The sentence becomes true. Page methods and tests are fully typed.
options.against: The reader of scaled_v_expr learns nothing about book::append (typed) or book::fill_random (the exception). The exception stays documented only in the other two places. The review named that as its second acceptable choice. It is less informative.

options.label: C
options.what: Replace the sentence with a reference only: "Who may take a packed address: Note [VNNI Packed V layout] in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp."
options.for: The rule then lives in one place. A third copy cannot go out of date again.
options.against: The scaled_v_expr reader loses the local summary of why the plane address appears here. The Note reference already sits on the line above (line 2247). So this option adds little.

final.recommended: A. The review asked for either naming the exception or dropping "book". Naming the exception and writing book::append makes the sentence exactly true for every caller of plane and pair_base, and it keeps the useful local summary. The word book alone would still read as a claim about every book method, even with the exception named. book::append is the one book method that goes through the typed route. So the sentence names it. Reusing the Note's wording ("fills a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates") keeps the three statements identical and avoids a new comment-vs-code mismatch (fill_storage_slot fills K directly and only the V plane through plane). The preferred option recorded in CONTEXT.md (the briefing file given to the agents that wrote this page) is to name fill_random as the exception. It agrees with the code.
final.reply: The review is right. book::fill_storage_slot takes the raw address of a block's packed V plane through v_vnni_access::plane. It then fills page_size * head_size elements (the whole plane) in a loop. No typed operation (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, at) is involved. The other two statements of the rule name book::fill_random as the exception. This sentence does not. I will replace it with: "Page methods, book::append and tests go through the typed operations instead. book::fill_random is the one documented exception: it fills a whole kv_block without interpreting coordinates (Note [VNNI Packed V layout])." The clause before it stays as written.

facts: PR #4697 ("Share KV row view helpers across cache callers") and PR #4698 ("Fix KV cache access across object boundaries") were opened by the maintainer against the branch jhan-kv-typed-tensors, the branch of PR #4557, not against main. Both are MERGED and GitHub reports the same merge commit, 8e0cf77bed, merged 2026-10-01 19:56 UTC [gh pr view 4697 / 4698 --json baseRefName,mergeCommit, run 2026-10-06].

The merge commit 8e0cf77bed is not an ancestor of main dd6e85226b (rc 1) and not an ancestor of the squashed PR head c5d44bd86f (rc 1). It is an ancestor of the pre-squash branch tip 1bdd592ff2 (rc 0). So the content of both PRs is inside the one squashed commit that this PR adds on top of main [git merge-base --is-ancestor, run in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-issue4525].

scaled_v_expr is the weighted sum of the software (AVX-512, non-AMX) attention path: it multiplies each token's V row by its attention weight and adds the rows up. On main its data pointer has type `const bf16s*`, where bf16s is a 16-element vector of bf16 values (bf16 = 16-bit brain floating point) [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2183; h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:20]. At the PR head the pointer has type `const bf16*`, one element [tron-issue4525 h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2166].

The PR rewrites the tile address in the three AVX-512 accumulate loops. main computes `reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) + chunk_offset` and loads `tile + k`, where bf16x32 is a 32-element vector and chunk_size is 16 [main kv_cache.hpp:2207-2210, 2276-2278, 2291-2293; h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17,51]. The head computes `data + i * head_size + 2 * chunk_size * chunk_offset` and loads `tile + 2 * chunk_size * k` [tron-issue4525 kv_cache.hpp:2190-2206, 2268-2272, 2282-2290]. Head sizes 256 and 512 reuse the 16-chunk helper [kv_cache.hpp:2300-2306].

The two address forms are the same bytes. One bf16s step is 16 elements, so `i * (head_size / 16)` vectors is `i * head_size` elements. One bf16x32 step is 32 elements, which is `2 * chunk_size`. So the rewrite changes the source form, not the addresses [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17,20,51; h/tron/simd/types.hpp:27].

fill_storage_slot (the test-fixture routine that fills one KV slot with random values) casts the block address to `bf16*` on main [main kv_cache.hpp:1616]. At the head it writes `block.k` with a range loop and reaches the V plane through `detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view())`, with no cast [tron-issue4525 kv_cache.hpp:1651-1655]. Both of these changes arrived through PR #4698 [git diff 8e0cf77bed^1 8e0cf77bed -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, 1 file, 72 insertions, 67 deletions].

PR #4697 (commit 8bbbb7c82d) added four names to v_vnni.hpp: the aliases const_v_row_view<T, Cols, Dma> and v_row_view<T, Cols, Dma> (a contiguous, aligned, unit-stride transfer row of Cols elements, the row that set_v reads and get_v writes, not packed storage) and the helper functions v_source_row<Cols, Dma>(const T*) and v_destination_row<Cols, Dma>(T*) that build them from a pointer without checking alignment or copying [tron-issue4525 h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:202-221; git diff 8bbbb7c82d^1 8bbbb7c82d, 8 files, 39 insertions, 43 deletions].

The four names have consumers: page::set_v / page::get_v signatures [kv_cache.hpp:1911, 1919, 1927, 1936, 2423, 2441, 2459, 2476], save_v_impl in model.hpp [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3169], the FPGA staging callback [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2761], and the tests t_llama_unit, t_amx_numerics, t_amx_dispatch_dtype and heterogeneous_scheduler_compile [grep over h src t at the head].

The live PR body credits both PRs in wording that does not say the merge target: line 43 'The V reads do the same since the maintainer's PR #4698 (merge commit 8e0cf77bed): scaled_v_expr and fill_storage_slot read bf16 arrays without a cast.' and line 44 '(... the aliases from the maintainer's PR #4697, defined in v_vnni.hpp)' [pr-body-live.md:43-44]. The v_vnni.hpp bullet (lines 34-40) does not list the four names [pr-body-live.md:34-40].

facts: PR #4697 ("Share KV row view helpers across cache callers") and PR #4698 ("Fix KV cache access across object boundaries") were opened by the maintainer against the branch jhan-kv-typed-tensors, the branch of PR #4557, not against main. Both are MERGED and GitHub reports the same merge commit, 8e0cf77bed, merged 2026-10-01 19:56 UTC [gh pr view 4697 / 4698 --json baseRefName,mergeCommit,mergedAt, run 2026-10-06].

The merge commit 8e0cf77bed is not an ancestor of main dd6e85226b (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` returns rc, return code, 1 = not an ancestor) and not an ancestor of the squashed PR head c5d44bd86f (rc 1). It is an ancestor of the pre-squash branch tip 1bdd592ff2 (rc 0 = ancestor). So the content of both PRs is inside the one squashed commit that this PR adds on top of main [git merge-base --is-ancestor, run in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-issue4525].

scaled_v_expr is the weighted sum of the software attention path (AVX-512, the 512-bit vector instruction set, as opposed to AMX, the tile matrix instruction set the attention kernels use). It multiplies each token's V row by its attention weight and adds the rows up. On main its data pointer has type `const bf16s*`, where bf16s is a 16-element vector of bf16 values (bf16 = 16-bit brain floating point) [main dd6e85226b h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2183, h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:20]. At the PR head the pointer has type `const bf16*`, one element [tron-issue4525 h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2166].

The PR rewrites the tile address (the start of the 32-element V segment that one accumulate step loads) in the three AVX-512 accumulate loops. main computes `tile = reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size))`, plus `+ chunk_offset` in the 16-chunk helper, and loads `tile + k`. bf16x32 is a 32-element vector and chunk_size is 16 (elements per vector register) [main kv_cache.hpp:2207-2210, 2276-2278, 2291-2293, h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17,51, h/tron/simd/types.hpp:27]. The head computes `tile = data + i * head_size`, plus `+ 2 * chunk_size * chunk_offset` in the helper, and loads `tile + 2 * chunk_size * k` [tron-issue4525 kv_cache.hpp:2190-2206, 2268-2272, 2282-2290]. Head sizes 256 and 512 reuse the 16-chunk helper [kv_cache.hpp:2300-2306].

The two address forms are the same bytes. One bf16s step is 16 elements, so `i * (head_size / 16)` vectors is `i * head_size` elements. One bf16x32 step is 32 elements, which is `2 * chunk_size`. So the rewrite changes the source form, not the addresses [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17,20,51, h/tron/simd/types.hpp:27].

The #4698 merge diff did more than the three loops that remain at the head. It also removed the cast in the constructor initializer (`data(reinterpret_cast<const bf16s*>(v_vnni_access::plane(v_page)))` became `data(v_vnni_access::plane(v_page))`, now [tron-issue4525 kv_cache.hpp:2257]), rewrote a fourth, 8-lane loop (`tile = data + i * (head_size / chunk_size) + part * 8` became `data + i * head_size + part * 8 * chunk_size`), and removed casts in set_v, get_v and the copy path [git diff 8e0cf77bed^1 8e0cf77bed -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, 1 file, 72 insertions, 67 deletions]. The 8-lane loop no longer exists at c5d44bd86f: main's PR #4726 removed the 8-lane build [pr-body-live.md:16, grep 'part \* 8' over kv_cache.hpp at the head = no hit].

fill_storage_slot (the test-fixture routine that fills one KV slot, one layer's key and value storage, with random values) casts the block address to `bf16*` on main [main kv_cache.hpp:1616]. At the head it writes `block.k` with a range loop and reaches the V plane (the packed V array of one block) through `detail::v_vnni_access::plane(block.v.as_view())`, with no cast [tron-issue4525 kv_cache.hpp:1651-1655]. This change arrived through PR #4698 [the same merge diff, deleted line `bf16* data = reinterpret_cast<bf16*>(&block);`].

PR #4697 (commit 8bbbb7c82d) added four names to v_vnni.hpp: the aliases const_v_row_view<T, Cols, Dma> and v_row_view<T, Cols, Dma> (Dma: whether the memory is DMA-reachable, DMA = direct memory access). Each is one contiguous, aligned, unit-stride (element step of one) transfer row of Cols elements, the row that set_v reads and get_v writes, not packed storage. The helper functions v_source_row<Cols, Dma>(const T*) and v_destination_row<Cols, Dma>(T*) build them from a pointer and neither check alignment nor copy [tron-issue4525 h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:202-221, git diff --stat 8bbbb7c82d^1 8bbbb7c82d, 8 files, 39 insertions, 43 deletions].

The four names have consumers: page::set_v / page::get_v signatures [kv_cache.hpp:1911, 1919, 1927, 1936, 2423, 2441, 2459, 2476], save_v_impl in model.hpp [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3169], the FPGA (field-programmable gate array, the hardware attention path) staging callback [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2761], and the tests t_llama_unit, t_amx_numerics, t_amx_dispatch_dtype and heterogeneous_scheduler_compile [grep over h src t at the head, 52 hits outside v_vnni.hpp].

The live PR body credits both PRs in wording that does not say the merge target: line 43 'The V reads do the same since the maintainer's PR #4698 (merge commit 8e0cf77bed): scaled_v_expr and fill_storage_slot read bf16 arrays without a cast.' and line 44 '(... the aliases from the maintainer's PR #4697, defined in v_vnni.hpp)' [pr-body-live.md:43-44]. Line 47 says only 'scaled_v_expr (the software path's weighted sum) takes the packed view.' [pr-body-live.md:47]. The v_vnni.hpp bullet (lines 34-40) does not list the four names [pr-body-live.md:34-40]. The squash commit message has the same wording: 'including the maintainer's PR 4697 ... and PR 4698' with no merge target [git log -1 c5d44bd86f, message lines 26-29].

The Verification section's instruction comparison is limited to 'the pre-rebase code' [pr-body-live.md:106]. A separate machine-code check of the #4698 change exists: objdump -d (the disassembler) of t_llama_unit, round r2 (the second verification round of the maintainer's review) on delphi-3bda (the Intel test machine with AMX), 2026-09-30. The 'after' binary was built from the local review tree a0e8d7155e, and the 'before' binary was the r1 (first verification round) binary built from the branch without the maintainer's change [exec/ben-20260930/r2-results.txt:1-3, 27-31].

The tree a0e8d7155e is not on the PR branch history. `git merge-base --is-ancestor a0e8d7155e 1bdd592ff2` returns rc 1. It is one commit below the last commit of the local ben-r2 history (ca372d9e9f, a comment-only commit that r2 did not rebuild): the PR branch at c73e7fb2f9, plus the maintainer's commits 63df10cf90 and 6b6bcbcb29 merged locally by c5d0c13672, plus three wording commits. The ben-r2 branch and worktree no longer exist, so these commits are reachable only by hash. [git log --oneline -8 a0e8d7155e]. 63df10cf90 is an ancestor of it (rc 0). So the r2 check covers the exact source change of #4698, but not the squashed head c5d44bd86f.

The r2 objdump compared only the head-size-128 instantiation. t_llama_unit holds two functions of scaled_v_expr<64, 128>, with 82 and 219 instructions in both binaries, identical after address normalisation (code addresses replaced by placeholders before the compare) [exec/ben-20260930/r2-results.txt:27-31]. The head-size-64 loop [kv_cache.hpp:2268] and the 16-chunk helper for head sizes 256 and 512 [kv_cache.hpp:2190] have no disassembly comparison. They rest on the element arithmetic above.

The 2026-10-06 token identity at c5d44bd86f against main dd6e85226b (seven arms, that is seven binary-plus-configuration combinations, one identical 256-token file) includes a kill-switch arm (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1). That arm runs the AVX-512 software path [pr-body-live.md:18, 129]. The software path calls `page.template scaled_v<geometry.kv>(...)` [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1964-1969], which returns a detail::scaled_v_expr [kv_cache.hpp:2388-2391, 2406]. The constructor's requires clause admits only head sizes 64, 128, 256 and 512 [kv_cache.hpp:2253-2254]. quote:
This line is new in this PR, and the description points reviewers away from it. "What changes" says "The V reads do the same since the maintainer's PR #4698 (merge commit 8e0cf77bed): `scaled_v_expr` and `fill_storage_slot` read `bf16` arrays without a cast", which reads as base state. `gh pr view 4697/4698` gives `baseRefName: jhan-kv-typed-tensors` for both, with the same merge commit, so they are maintainer contributions *into this branch*, and their content is part of this diff against `main`. At `dd6e85226b` — the base the Status section names — `scaled_v_expr` still declares `const bf16s* const data;` and `fill_storage_slot` still does `bf16* data = reinterpret_cast<bf16*>(&block);`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8e0cf77bed dd6e85226b` returns 1.

Why that matters beyond bookkeeping: changing `data` from `bf16s*` to `bf16*` re-derived the tile addressing in all three AVX-512 accumulate paths — base `reinterpret_cast<const bf16x32*>(data + i * (head_size / chunk_size)) + chunk_offset` with `tile + k`, head `data + i * head_size + 2 * chunk_size * chunk_offset` with `tile + 2 * chunk_size * k`. The arithmetic checks out, but it is the most delicate index math in the diff, and the only description line touching it is "`scaled_v_expr` (the software path's weighted sum) takes the packed view." The Verification section's instruction comparison is the right evidence, but it is scoped to "the pre-rebase code", so it does not stand in for saying plainly that this PR rewrote the loops.

Please keep the credit to the maintainer but say that #4697 and #4698 merged into this branch rather than into `main`, and describe the `scaled_v_expr` addressing rewrite and the `fill_storage_slot` cast removal as changes of this PR. The `const_v_row_view` / `v_row_view` sentence has the same wording problem, and those four aliases are also missing from the `v_vnni.hpp` bullet's list of the header's contents.

facts: DMA memory (memory an FPGA can read and write directly) is handed out by dma_allocate_aligned, a function in h/system/memory.hpp. In production it returns memory from the process heap object (heap->allocate or the v2 arena heap), not from malloc and not from a function named operator new [src/system/memory.cpp:460-468].

In C++, objects of an implicit-lifetime type (a type with a trivial constructor and destructor, for example a plain struct of integers) may come into existence without a constructor call. This happens only through a short list of operations: a call of a function named operator new or operator new[], malloc and its relatives, memcpy and memmove, bit_cast, and starting the lifetime of an unsigned char or std::byte array. The Note in the header repeats this list [h/system/memory.hpp:171-178].

std::memset is not on that list. The list names memcpy and memmove and nothing else from the C string library [h/system/memory.hpp:176-177; external source: N4950 (the C++23 draft) [intro.object]/13 and [cstring.syn]/3].

For a trivially constructible element type, the two make_unique_dma templates write zeros with std::memset and run no constructor [h/system/memory.hpp:252-253, 268-269]. The two make_unique_dma_for_overwrite templates write nothing for such a type [h/system/memory.hpp:287-288, 300-302].

The DMA descriptor ring allocates its descriptors with make_unique_dma<dma_desc_t[]>(sz) and then writes d->desc_idx = index into each one [src/pos/dma_ring.cpp:39, 47]. The DMA queue allocates its head word with make_unique_dma<dma_queue_head>() [h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:213-214].

dma_desc_t is a 32-byte struct of integer and bit-field members with no constructor or destructor [h/pos/dma/common.hpp:41-60]. dma_queue_head is a union of a bit-field struct and one uint32_t with no user-declared special members [h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:19-27]. The Note mentions neither the four templates nor these callers. It names the KV book as the only reader of unconstructed objects and try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite as the one function routed through the wrapper [h/system/memory.hpp:169-170, 183-185].

facts: DMA memory (memory the FPGA, the accelerator card, can read and write directly) is handed out by dma_allocate_aligned, a function in h/system/memory.hpp. In production it returns memory from the process heap object (heap->allocate or the v2 heap (the second heap implementation)), not from malloc and not from a function named operator new [src/system/memory.cpp:460-469].

In C++, objects of an implicit-lifetime type (a type with a trivial constructor and destructor, for example a plain struct of integers) may come into existence without a constructor call. This happens only through a short list of operations: a call of a function named operator new or operator new[], malloc and its relatives, memcpy and memmove, bit_cast, and starting the lifetime of an unsigned char or std::byte array. The Note (the comment block "Note [DMA allocation creates objects]" at h/system/memory.hpp:167-195) repeats this list [h/system/memory.hpp:171-178].

std::memset is not on that list. The list names memcpy and memmove and nothing else from the C string library [h/system/memory.hpp:176-177, external source: N4950 (the C++23 draft) [intro.object]/13 and [cstring.syn]/3, as recalled, not read locally in this session].

The PR adds a tag type dma_allocation_t (an empty type whose only job is to select this overload) and a global function named operator new[] that forwards to dma_allocate_aligned [h/system/memory.hpp:157-163, 196-201]. Only one template calls it: try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T[]>, the allocation that may fail, used by the KV book (the per-model store of attention keys and values) [h/system/memory.hpp:380-382, callers h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1289, 1424, 1434].

Four sibling templates in the same header still call dma_allocate_aligned directly. They are make_unique_dma<T> [h/system/memory.hpp:251], make_unique_dma<T[]> [266], make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T> [286] and make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T[]> [298]. The PR does not change these lines. They are main dd6e85226b's code, where they sit at lines 202, 217, 237 and 249 [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- h/system/memory.hpp, git show dd6e85226b:h/system/memory.hpp].

The PR diff of the header has three hunks (changed blocks): one added `#include <new>` line, the tag/Note/wrapper block, and the one rerouted call site (52 insertions, 1 deletion) [git diff dd6e85226b c5d44bd86f -- h/system/memory.hpp].

For a trivially constructible element type, the two make_unique_dma templates write zeros with std::memset and run no constructor [h/system/memory.hpp:252-253, 268-269]. The two make_unique_dma_for_overwrite templates write nothing for such a type [h/system/memory.hpp:287-288, 300-302].

Two production callers that the reviewer named pass a class type (a struct or union) through those templates. The DMA descriptor ring allocates its descriptors with make_unique_dma<dma_desc_t[]>(sz) and then writes d->desc_idx = index into each one [src/pos/dma_ring.cpp:39, 47]. The DMA queue allocates its head word with make_unique_dma<dma_queue_head>() [h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:213-214].

dma_desc_t is a 32-byte struct of integer and bit-field members with no constructor or destructor [h/pos/dma/common.hpp:42-60]. dma_queue_head is a union of a bit-field struct and one uint32_t with no user-declared special members [h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:19-27]. Both are implicit-lifetime types. The object-creation rule the Note applies to kv_block (the KV book's storage block type) applies to them as well.

The reviewer's list of class-typed callers is not complete. dmatensor's element type Scalar is constrained to bf16 or fp16 by `concept dmascalar_t = one_of_t<T, bf16, fp16>` [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:25]. bf16 and fp16 are structs with one scalar member and a defaulted default constructor (`constexpr bf16() noexcept = default;`), so they are trivially constructible class types [h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp:12-21, h/common/numerics/fp16.hpp:10-19]. The six dmatensor call sites therefore take the memset or write-nothing branches [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:181, 186, 191, 207, 248, 273].

The one other class-typed caller is not affected. tensor.hpp allocates make_unique_dma<strip[]> [h/tron/hardware/tensor.hpp:107]. strip has the user-provided constructor `strip() noexcept : scales(), groups() {}` [h/tron/hardware/weight_format.hpp:26-32]. So make_unique_dma takes the placement-new loop for it, and that loop creates the objects [h/system/memory.hpp:270-272].

The Note mentions neither the four templates nor these callers. It names the KV book as the only reader of unconstructed objects and try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite as the one function routed through the wrapper [h/system/memory.hpp:169-170, 183-186]. The paragraph that names that function ends at line 186 ("constructor."), and line 187 is a blank comment line.

The unit-test build replaces dma_allocate_aligned with a stand-in function that calls aligned_alloc. aligned_alloc is on the list. So no test can detect a caller that stays on the direct path, as the Note's last paragraph says [src/pos/fake.cpp:439-444, h/system/memory.hpp:192-195].

The other reviewer's resolved thread on line 192 asked for the maintainer's explicit sign-off on the operator new[] approach. The approach came from this branch's commit 39a6899446, not from the maintainer's PR #4698 [exec/wade-20261005/skill/wade-inline-4557.md:10-11]. The maintainer's recorded review state is CHANGES_REQUESTED (2026-09-29). He has posted no review since that day [gh pr view 4557 --json reviews].

quote: Not for this PR, but worth one sentence or a tracking issue. The Note reaches an unqualified verdict about the header's base allocator — "dma_allocate_aligned is not on that list. It is an ordinary function that calls none of them, so the memory it returns holds no objects" — and then concludes for one function. Four sibling templates in the same header still call `dma_allocate_aligned` directly: `make_unique_dma<T>` (line 251) and `make_unique_dma<T[]>` (266), whose trivially-constructible branch writes only `std::memset`, which is not an implicit-object-creation operation ([cstring.syn] names memcpy and memmove), and `make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T>` (286) and `make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T[]>` (298), which write nothing at all. So the same argument reaches class-typed callers of those four — src/pos/dma_ring.cpp:39 `return make_unique_dma<dma_desc_t[]>(sz);  // 0 initializes`, whose descriptors are then written through `d->desc_idx = index;` at line 47, and h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:214 `make_unique_dma<dma_queue_head>()`. I am not asking for them to be rerouted here; a sentence saying the wrapper covers the KV-book path, with an issue alongside #4588, would stop the next reader of line 180 from having to work out why the four functions seventy lines below contradict it. Given @Wado-posi's open question at line 192, this is probably best settled once @bgamari-positron has signed off on the `operator new[]` approach, since it extends exactly that mechanism.
